title: Commitment-lease driven proactive drain for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers buying regional dedicated capacity need (1) enforceable throughput commitments tied to contracts, (2) predictable latency SLOs during partial zone outages, and (3) strong guarantees that traffic serving data subject to residency requirements will not be served from non-authorized regions. Current placement and autoscale semantics either immediately spill traffic to any available region on capacity pressure (breaking residency guarantees) or rigidly refuse spill (causing sustained SLA breaches).

Proposed solution: introduce a Commitment Lease abstraction on dedicated pools. A commitment lease is a short-lived, negotiable token attached to reserved throughput that provides a controlled handoff path when a zone or fleet becomes constrained. Instead of immediate cross-region spill, the allocator will (a) attempt local recovery (prefetch/warm), (b) enter a controlled soft-drain window where remaining capacity is throttled to preserve latency SLOs, and (c) if the lease cannot be honored within the window, trigger a prioritized, residency-aware spillover policy that respects contract tiers and data residency rules.

Goals:
- Preserve contractually promised throughput as long as feasible without violating data residency constraints.
- Reduce visible latency/regression during transient zone disturbances via adaptive throttling and fast prewarm.
- Provide observable, auditable transitions for customer SLAs and compliance reviews.

Scope included in this ticket:
- Commitment Lease model (token lifecycle, TTLs, renegotiation semantics).
- Allocator changes to consult lease state in placement decisions.
- Autoscaler hooks to honor lease-backed short-term scale requests and prewarm signaling.
- Admission-control throttle that steps through graceful degradation phases: protection, soft-drain, spill.
- Console telemetry (per-lease metrics, transition events) and incident runbook notes.

Out of scope (future tickets): fine-grained billing reconciliation of partially honored leases, cross-tenant burst-sharing during failure windows.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment lease object exists in datastore with create/read/update/delete and TTL semantics
Allocator consults lease state when deciding to place or spill requests and emits deposit/renew/evict events
Autoscaler responds to lease-backed prewarm signals within configured SLO (90% of prewarm requests start containers within 30s in staging)
System enforces residency constraints: no traffic flagged with residency=EU is directed to non-EU regions during any transition
Console shows lease lifecycle events and a per-customer commitment dashboard for at least one internal demo customer
E2E chaos test: simulated single AZ network partition results in soft-drain -> prewarm -> either local recovery or controlled spill with correct audit trail
comments: 2025-02-10 Alyssa Chen: Initial draft — outlining commitment lease concept after customer postmortem. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/commitment-leases (draft) and incident notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/incident-2025-01-22-summary.pdf

2025-02-11 Diego Martínez: Added rough TTL semantics (default 5m soft window, renewable once) and proposed allocator hook points. Flagging potential perf risk in high-churn fleets — will prototype with a lightweight in-memory lease cache to avoid datastore hot paths.

2025-02-12 Priya Kapoor (PM): This aligns with current enterprise contract ask. Please ensure telemetry surfaces per-commitment SLA breaches for billing & legal. Add a flag to make lease behavior opt-in per-customer until rollout is validated.

2025-02-13 Marco Ruiz (Design): Suggested UX flows for Console: a timeline for lease events and an ability to pin a lease to an SLA document. We should mock an alert that explains "why" traffic spilled (capacity vs residency).

2025-02-14 Diego Martínez: Prototype notes — implemented lease cache and allocator stub in branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2147. Early perf bench (staging) shows ~3% median allocation latency increase under 1000 rps; will optimize with batch lookups.

2025-02-15 QA (Emma Li): Test plan added to the ticket. Will include a chaos scenario with delayed renewals and an audit check for residency enforcement. Need a mock enterprise customer with EU-only residency.

2025-02-16 Security (Noah Patel): Security review requested. Concerns: lease tokens must be signed and immutable to prevent tampering; store minimal PII. Recommend HSM-backed signing for GA (can start with KMS dev keys for prototype).

2025-02-17 Diego Martínez: Changed default softness window to 4m (from 5m) after benches and added ability to extend by up to 2m via autoscaler hook. Updated branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2163

2025-02-18 Alyssa Chen: PM approval to proceed to implementation sprint 2025-W08 with opt-in flag. Added rollout plan and customer communication draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/commitment-leases-rollout
